records.source: אַחַר֙ הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה כְּשֹׁ֕ךְ חֲמַ֖ת הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ אֲחַשְׁוֵר֑וֹשׁ זָכַ֤ר אֶת־וַשְׁתִּי֙ וְאֵ֣ת אֲשֶׁר־עָשָׂ֔תָה וְאֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר־נִגְזַ֖ר עָלֶֽיהָ׃
records.gloss: After the things the these, as subsided [the] rage of the king Ahasuerus, he remembered Vashti and what she had done and what had been decreed against her.
pieces: Some time later, when the anger of King Ahasuerus had cooled, he remembered Vashti and what she had done and what had been decreed against her.

L.1: After these things, when the rage of King Ahasuerus had subsided, he remembered Vashti and what she had done and what had been decreed against her.

R.1: Later, after King Ahasuerus was no longer angry, he thought about Vashti. He remembered what she had done and the order he had made against her.

decisions.choice: after these things: some time after the events of chapter 1
decisions.reason: The phrase moves the story on without saying how long. Verse 16 dates Esther's coming to the king to his seventh year, four years after the feast of 1:3.

decisions.choice: he remembered Vashti: he thought of her again
alternatives: he called to mind her offense
decisions.reason: The verb means to call to mind; it can carry longing or regret, but the text does not say what the king felt. The verse then names both what she did and what was decreed, setting her offense and his own decree side by side.

decisions.choice: what had been decreed against her: by the irrevocable law of 1:19
decisions.reason: The verb means to cut, and so to decide or decree. Whatever the king now felt, the law of Persia and Media could not be undone.

decisions.choice: had cooled (Balanced); was no longer angry (Readable)
decisions.reason: The verb is used of water subsiding (Genesis 8:1) and again of the king's anger in 7:10.

records.heading: A search for a new queen

records.source: וַיֹּאמְר֥וּ נַעֲרֵֽי־הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ מְשָׁרְתָ֑יו יְבַקְשׁ֥וּ לַמֶּ֛לֶךְ נְעָר֥וֹת בְּתוּל֖וֹת טוֹב֥וֹת מַרְאֶֽה׃
records.gloss: And said [the] young men of the king, his servants, Let them seek for the king young women, virgins, good of appearance.
pieces: Then the king's young attendants who served him said, "Let a search be made for beautiful young virgins for the king.

L.2: And the young men of the king, his attendants, said, "Let them seek young women for the king, virgins good of appearance.

R.2: So the young men who served the king said to him, "Your Majesty, let a search be made for beautiful young women who have never married.

decisions.choice: the young men of the king: his personal attendants
decisions.reason: The word for "young man" also means a servant or attendant; here it is the men who wait on the king (6:3, 5).

decisions.choice: young women, virgins: unmarried girls who had not had relations with a man
decisions.reason: The two words together stress youth and virginity. The proposal answers the end of 1:19, a woman "better than she".

decisions.choice: virgins (Literal, Balanced); young women who have never married (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable says what the word means in this setting in plain words.

records.source: וְיַפְקֵ֨ד הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ פְּקִידִים֮ בְּכָל־מְדִינ֣וֹת מַלְכוּתוֹ֒ וְיִקְבְּצ֣וּ אֶת־כָּל־נַעֲרָֽה־בְ֠תוּלָה טוֹבַ֨ת מַרְאֶ֜ה אֶל־שׁוּשַׁ֤ן הַבִּירָה֙ אֶל־בֵּ֣ית הַנָּשִׁ֔ים אֶל־יַ֥ד הֵגֶ֛א סְרִ֥יס הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ שֹׁמֵ֣ר הַנָּשִׁ֑ים וְנָת֖וֹן תַּמְרוּקֵיהֶֽן׃
records.gloss: And let appoint the king appointees in all [the] provinces of his kingdom, and let them gather every young woman, virgin, good of appearance, to Susa the citadel, to the house of the women, into [the] hand of Hegai, eunuch of the king, keeper of the women; and let be given their cosmetics.
pieces: Let the king appoint officers in all the provinces of his kingdom to gather every beautiful young virgin to the harem in the citadel of Susa. Let them be put in the care of Hegai, the king's eunuch who is in charge of the women, and let them be given their beauty treatments.

L.3: And let the king appoint officers in all the provinces of his kingdom, and let them gather every young woman, a virgin good of appearance, to Susa the citadel, to the house of the women, into the hand of Hegai the king's eunuch, keeper of the women, and let their cosmetics be given [them].

R.3: You could choose officers in every province of your kingdom to bring all the beautiful young women to the women's quarters in the royal fortress in Susa. Hegai, the king's official in charge of the women, would take care of them and give them beauty treatments.

decisions.choice: the house of the women: the harem, the quarters of the king's wives and concubines
decisions.reason: Persian kings kept many women in separate quarters of the palace, guarded by eunuchs (verse 14). The young women were taken there, not only invited.

decisions.choice: into the hand of Hegai: into his care and under his authority
decisions.reason: "Hand" stands for charge or custody, as in verses 8 and 14.

decisions.choice: cosmetics: ointments and treatments for beauty
decisions.reason: The word is from a root meaning to scrape or rub, and so to cleanse or polish. Verse 12 describes the year-long treatment with oils and perfumes.

decisions.choice: appointees: officials named for a task
decisions.reason: The noun comes from the verb before it, "appoint"; the same word is used for Joseph's advice to Pharaoh (Genesis 41:34).

decisions.choice: the house of the women (Literal); the harem (Balanced); the women's quarters (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced uses the common English word; Readable uses a plainer phrase.

records.source: וְהַֽנַּעֲרָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֤ר תִּיטַב֙ בְּעֵינֵ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ תִּמְלֹ֖ךְ תַּ֣חַת וַשְׁתִּ֑י וַיִּיטַ֧ב הַדָּבָ֛ר בְּעֵינֵ֥י הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ וַיַּ֥עַשׂ כֵּֽן׃ס
records.gloss: And the young woman who will be good in [the] eyes of the king, let her reign instead of Vashti. And was good the word in [the] eyes of the king, and he did so.
pieces: Then let the young woman who pleases the king become queen instead of Vashti." The king liked this advice, and he did so.

L.4: And let the young woman who is good in the eyes of the king reign instead of Vashti." And the word was good in the eyes of the king, and he did so.

R.4: Then the young woman the king likes best can become queen in Vashti's place." The king liked this idea, so he did what they said.

decisions.choice: good in the eyes of the king: pleasing to the king
decisions.reason: The same phrase is used for the girl and for the advice: the king chooses by what pleases him, as in 1:21.

decisions.choice: let her reign: let her become queen
decisions.reason: The verb is "be king" or "reign"; for the king's wife it means to have the rank of queen (verse 17).

records.source: אִ֣ישׁ יְהוּדִ֔י הָיָ֖ה בְּשׁוּשַׁ֣ן הַבִּירָ֑ה וּשְׁמ֣וֹ מָרְדֳּכַ֗י בֶּ֣ן יָאִ֧יר בֶּן־שִׁמְעִ֛י בֶּן־קִ֖ישׁ אִ֥ישׁ יְמִינִֽי׃
records.gloss: A man, a Jew, there was in Susa the citadel, and his name [was] Mordecai, son of Jair, son of Shimei, son of Kish, a man of Benjamin,
pieces: Now there was a Jew in the citadel of Susa named Mordecai son of Jair, son of Shimei, son of Kish, a Benjaminite,

L.5: There was a man, a Jew, in Susa the citadel, and his name was Mordecai, son of Jair, son of Shimei, son of Kish, a Benjaminite,

R.5: Now in the royal fortress in Susa there was a Jew named Mordecai. He was from the tribe of Benjamin. His father was Jair, Jair's father was Shimei, and Shimei's father was Kish.

decisions.choice: a Jew: a member of the Jewish people, though from the tribe of Benjamin
decisions.reason: The word first meant a man of Judah, the tribe and the kingdom. After the exile it came to mean anyone of the people of Israel who had come from the kingdom of Judah, and so it can describe a Benjaminite. In Esther it names the people as a whole: "the Jews".

decisions.choice: Shimei, Kish, Benjaminite: names from the family of King Saul
decisions.reason: Kish was the father of Saul, Israel's first king, a Benjaminite (1 Samuel 9:1-2), and Shimei was a Benjaminite of Saul's clan (2 Samuel 16:5). The names may be Mordecai's actual ancestors or a way of naming his clan. Either way the reader is invited to remember that Saul fought Agag, king of Amalek (1 Samuel 15), when Haman "the Agagite" appears (3:1).

decisions.choice: Mordecai: a Babylonian name
decisions.reason: The name is formed from Marduk, the chief god of Babylon. Jews in exile often bore a local name, as Daniel and his friends were given Babylonian names (Daniel 1:7).

decisions.choice: Readable names the tribe first and spells out the line of fathers
decisions.reason: A string of "son of" can confuse a new reader; Readable gives the same names as plain sentences.

records.heading: Mordecai and Esther

records.source: אֲשֶׁ֤ר הָגְלָה֙ מִיר֣וּשָׁלַ֔יִם עִם־הַגֹּלָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָגְלְתָ֔ה עִ֖ם יְכָנְיָ֣ה מֶֽלֶךְ־יְהוּדָ֑ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר הֶגְלָ֔ה נְבוּכַדְנֶאצַּ֖ר מֶ֥לֶךְ בָּבֶֽל׃
records.gloss: who had been exiled from Jerusalem with the exiles which had been exiled with Jeconiah king of Judah, whom had exiled Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon.
pieces: who had been carried into exile from Jerusalem among the captives taken away with Jeconiah king of Judah, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had deported.

L.6: who had been taken into exile from Jerusalem with the exiles who were taken into exile with Jeconiah king of Judah, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had taken into exile.

R.6: Mordecai's family had been taken away from Jerusalem as prisoners. They were among the people whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon took away with Jehoiachin king of Judah.

decisions.choice: who had been exiled: Mordecai's family, in the person of his ancestor
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "who" most simply refers to Mordecai. But the exile with Jeconiah was in 597 BC, more than a hundred years before Xerxes, so the clause is best taken of his great-grandfather Kish, or of the family as a whole, which went into exile and remained there.

decisions.choice: Jeconiah, Nebuchadnezzar: the exile of 597 BC
decisions.reason: Jeconiah, also called Jehoiachin, was taken to Babylon with the leading people of Jerusalem (2 Kings 24:10-16; Jeremiah 24:1). The verb "exile" is repeated four times, stressing that this family belonged to the exiles who did not return.

decisions.choice: Jeconiah (Literal, Balanced); Jehoiachin (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable uses the form of the king's name found in 2 Kings, which a reader is more likely to know.

records.source: וַיְהִ֨י אֹמֵ֜ן אֶת־הֲדַסָּ֗ה הִ֤יא אֶסְתֵּר֙ בַּת־דֹּד֔וֹ כִּ֛י אֵ֥ין לָ֖הּ אָ֣ב וָאֵ֑ם וְהַנַּעֲרָ֤ה יְפַת־תֹּ֨אַר֙ וְטוֹבַ֣ת מַרְאֶ֔ה וּבְמ֤וֹת אָבִ֨יהָ֙ וְאִמָּ֔הּ לְקָחָ֧הּ מָרְדֳּכַ֛י ל֖וֹ לְבַֽת׃
records.gloss: And he was bringing up Hadassah, she [is] Esther, [the] daughter of his uncle, for there was not to her father and mother; and the young woman [was] beautiful of form and good of appearance; and at [the] death of her father and her mother, took her Mordecai for himself as a daughter.
pieces: He had brought up Hadassah, that is, Esther, his uncle's daughter, because she had neither father nor mother. The young woman had a lovely figure and was beautiful to look at. When her father and mother died, Mordecai took her in as his own daughter.

L.7: And he was bringing up Hadassah, that is Esther, the daughter of his uncle, for she had no father or mother. And the young woman was beautiful of form and good of appearance, and when her father and her mother died, Mordecai took her for himself as a daughter.

R.7: Mordecai had a cousin named Hadassah, who was also called Esther. Her father and mother had died, so Mordecai adopted her and raised her as his own daughter. She had a lovely figure and a beautiful face.

decisions.choice: Hadassah, that is Esther: her Hebrew and her other name
decisions.reason: Hadassah means "myrtle". Esther is probably from the Persian word for "star", though some link it with the Babylonian goddess Ishtar. Like Mordecai, she bears a name of the empire besides her own.

decisions.choice: bringing up: caring for and raising as a guardian
decisions.reason: The verb is used of a foster parent or guardian (Numbers 11:12; 2 Kings 10:1). Verse 20 uses a related noun for her upbringing under Mordecai.

decisions.choice: the daughter of his uncle: his cousin
decisions.reason: Verse 15 names her father as Abihail, Mordecai's uncle. Taking her "as a daughter" means he raised her as his own.

decisions.choice: Readable tells of the adoption before her beauty
decisions.reason: Readable puts the facts of her family together and then describes her, to keep its sentences simple.

records.source: וַיְהִ֗י בְּהִשָּׁמַ֤ע דְּבַר־הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ וְדָת֔וֹ וּֽבְהִקָּבֵ֞ץ נְעָר֥וֹת רַבּ֛וֹת אֶל־שׁוּשַׁ֥ן הַבִּירָ֖ה אֶל־יַ֣ד הֵגָ֑י וַתִּלָּקַ֤ח אֶסְתֵּר֙ אֶל־בֵּ֣ית הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ אֶל־יַ֥ד הֵגַ֖י שֹׁמֵ֥ר הַנָּשִֽׁים׃
records.gloss: And it was, when was heard [the] word of the king and his law, and when were gathered young women many to Susa the citadel into [the] hand of Hegai, and was taken Esther to [the] house of the king, into [the] hand of Hegai, keeper of the women.
pieces: So when the king's command and his decree were proclaimed and many young women were gathered to the citadel of Susa and put in the care of Hegai, Esther too was taken to the king's palace and put in the care of Hegai, who was in charge of the women.

L.8: And it came about, when the word of the king and his law were heard, and when many young women were gathered to Susa the citadel into the hand of Hegai, that Esther was taken to the king's house, into the hand of Hegai, keeper of the women.

R.8: When the king's order was announced, many young women were brought to the royal fortress in Susa, and Hegai took charge of them. Esther was also taken to the king's palace and put under the care of Hegai, the man in charge of the women.

decisions.choice: Esther was taken: a passive verb, with no word on her own wishes
decisions.reason: The text does not say whether Esther went willingly. The same verb is used of the women gathered by royal order, and in verse 16.

decisions.choice: his law: the royal decree of verses 3-4
decisions.reason: The word is dat, the royal law or decree (1:8, 19).

decisions.choice: put in the care of Hegai
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "into the hand of" means here, as in verse 3.

records.source: וַתִּיטַ֨ב הַנַּעֲרָ֣ה בְעֵינָיו֮ וַתִּשָּׂ֣א חֶ֣סֶד לְפָנָיו֒ וַ֠יְבַהֵל אֶת־תַּמְרוּקֶ֤יהָ וְאֶת־מָנוֹתֶ֨הָ֙ לָתֵ֣ת לָ֔הּ וְאֵת֙ שֶׁ֣בַע הַנְּעָר֔וֹת הָרְאֻי֥וֹת לָֽתֶת־לָ֖הּ מִבֵּ֣ית הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיְשַׁנֶּ֧הָ וְאֶת־נַעֲרוֹתֶ֛יהָ לְט֖וֹב בֵּ֥ית הַנָּשִֽׁים׃
records.gloss: And was good the young woman in his eyes, and she won kindness before him; and he hastened her cosmetics and her portions to give to her, and the seven [of] the young women, the chosen to give to her from [the] house of the king; and he moved her and her young women to [the] best of [the] house of the women.
pieces: The young woman pleased Hegai and won his favor. He quickly provided her with her beauty treatments and her special food, and he gave her seven young women chosen from the king's palace to serve her. Then he moved her and her attendants to the best place in the harem.

L.9: And the young woman was good in his eyes, and she won kindness before him. And he hurried to give her her cosmetics and her portions, and the seven young women chosen to be given to her from the king's house, and he moved her and her young women to the best [place] of the house of the women.

R.9: Hegai liked Esther, and he was kind to her. He quickly began her beauty treatments and gave her special food. He chose seven young women from the king's palace to be her servants. Then he moved her and her servants into the best rooms in the women's quarters.

decisions.choice: she won kindness before him: she gained his favor
decisions.reason: The word chesed often means loyal, covenant love, but here, with "win" or "carry" and a superior who shows it, it means the kindness and goodwill he showed her (compare 2:17, where it is paired with "favor"). Esther wins the goodwill of all who meet her (verse 15).

decisions.choice: her portions: her allowance of food
decisions.reason: The word means a share or portion, often of food (1 Samuel 1:4; Daniel 1:5). The text does not say whether Esther kept Jewish food laws, as Daniel did; it does not raise the question.

decisions.choice: the chosen: the seven attendants were picked for her
alternatives: the appropriate seven, the usual allowance
decisions.reason: The word means "seen" and so "selected" or "fit". Seven attendants mark the favor shown her.

decisions.choice: kindness (Literal); favor (Balanced); he was kind to her (Readable)
decisions.reason: The project's usual "steadfast love" or "faithful love" for chesed would mislead here, where it is a courtier's goodwill toward a young woman in his care. The meaning decision gives the reason.

records.source: לֹא־הִגִּ֣ידָה אֶסְתֵּ֔ר אֶת־עַמָּ֖הּ וְאֶת־מֽוֹלַדְתָּ֑הּ כִּ֧י מָרְדֳּכַ֛י צִוָּ֥ה עָלֶ֖יהָ אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹא־תַגִּֽיד׃
records.gloss: Not had told Esther her people and her kindred, for Mordecai had commanded her that not she should tell.
pieces: Esther had not revealed her nationality or her family background, because Mordecai had told her not to.

L.10: Esther had not made known her people or her kindred, for Mordecai had commanded her that she should not make [it] known.

R.10: Esther had not told anyone that she was Jewish or who her family was, because Mordecai had told her not to.

decisions.choice: her people and her kindred: that she was a Jew and who her family was
decisions.reason: "People" is her nation; "kindred" is her family or clan. The secret matters later, when Haman's plot is against "her people" (7:3-4).

decisions.choice: Mordecai had commanded her: the text gives no reason
decisions.reason: The narrator does not say why Mordecai wanted her nationality hidden; it may have been caution about how the Jews were viewed (compare 3:8). Verse 20 repeats the point.

records.source: וּבְכָל־י֣וֹם וָי֔וֹם מָרְדֳּכַי֙ מִתְהַלֵּ֔ךְ לִפְנֵ֖י חֲצַ֣ר בֵּית־הַנָּשִׁ֑ים לָדַ֨עַת֙ אֶת־שְׁל֣וֹם אֶסְתֵּ֔ר וּמַה־יֵּעָשֶׂ֖ה בָּֽהּ׃
records.gloss: And on every day and day Mordecai [was] walking before [the] court of [the] house of the women, to know the welfare of Esther and what was being done with her.
pieces: Every day Mordecai walked back and forth in front of the court of the harem to find out how Esther was and what was happening to her.

L.11: And every day Mordecai walked back and forth in front of the court of the house of the women, to know how Esther was and what was being done with her.

R.11: Every day Mordecai walked back and forth near the courtyard of the women's quarters. He wanted to know how Esther was doing and what was happening to her.

decisions.choice: the welfare of Esther: how she was
decisions.reason: The word is shalom, "peace, well-being"; "to know the shalom of" someone is to ask after how they are (Genesis 37:14).

decisions.choice: walking: walking about, regularly and for some time
decisions.reason: The verb form means to walk to and fro; with "every day" it shows his steady care for her.

records.source: וּבְהַגִּ֡יעַ תֹּר֩ נַעֲרָ֨ה וְנַעֲרָ֜ה לָב֣וֹא׀אֶל־הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ אֲחַשְׁוֵר֗וֹשׁ מִקֵּץ֩ הֱי֨וֹת לָ֜הּ כְּדָ֤ת הַנָּשִׁים֙ שְׁנֵ֣ים עָשָׂ֣ר חֹ֔דֶשׁ כִּ֛י כֵּ֥ן יִמְלְא֖וּ יְמֵ֣י מְרוּקֵיהֶ֑ן שִׁשָּׁ֤ה חֳדָשִׁים֙ בְּשֶׁ֣מֶן הַמֹּ֔ר וְשִׁשָּׁ֤ה חֳדָשִׁים֙ בַּבְּשָׂמִ֔ים וּבְתַמְרוּקֵ֖י הַנָּשִֽׁים׃
records.gloss: And when arrived [the] turn of young woman and young woman to go in to the king Ahasuerus, after being for her according to [the] law of the women twelve months (for so were completed [the] days of their rubbings: six months with oil of myrrh and six months with spices and with [the] cosmetics of the women),
pieces: Each young woman's turn to go in to King Ahasuerus came after she had completed twelve months under the regulations for the women, since this was the full length of their beauty treatment: six months with oil of myrrh and six months with perfumes and cosmetics for women.

L.12: And when the turn of each young woman came to go in to King Ahasuerus, after she had been twelve months under the regulation for the women (for so the days of their beauty treatments were completed: six months with oil of myrrh, and six months with spices and with the cosmetics of the women),

R.12: Before a young woman could go to King Ahasuerus, she had to complete twelve months of beauty treatments, as the rules for the women required. For six months her skin was treated with oil of myrrh, and for six months with perfumes and creams.

decisions.choice: the law of the women: the regulations of the harem
decisions.reason: The word is dat again (1:8); even the women's year of preparation was laid down by rule.

decisions.choice: oil of myrrh, spices: costly perfumes and ointments
decisions.reason: Myrrh is a fragrant resin from Arabia and East Africa, used for perfume and anointing (Song of Songs 5:5; Psalm 45:9). The word for spices also means perfumes in general.

decisions.choice: for so were completed: a comment inside the sentence
decisions.reason: The words in parentheses explain the twelve months; the main sentence continues in verse 13. The same word for treatments is "cosmetics" in verses 3 and 9.

decisions.choice: her skin was treated (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable says what the oils were for; the word for the treatments means rubbing or massaging.

records.source: וּבָזֶ֕ה הַֽנַּעֲרָ֖ה בָּאָ֣ה אֶל־הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ אֵת֩ כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֨ר תֹּאמַ֜ר יִנָּ֤תֵֽן לָהּ֙ לָב֣וֹא עִמָּ֔הּ מִבֵּ֥ית הַנָּשִׁ֖ים עַד־בֵּ֥ית הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃
records.gloss: and in this [way] the young woman [was] going in to the king: all that she would say would be given to her to go with her from [the] house of the women to [the] house of the king.
pieces: This is how each young woman went in to the king: whatever she asked for was given to her to take with her from the harem to the king's palace.

L.13: and in this way the young woman would go in to the king: everything that she asked for would be given to her to go with her from the house of the women to the house of the king.

R.13: When it was a young woman's turn to go to the king, she could take with her from the women's quarters anything she asked for.

decisions.choice: all that she would say: whatever she asked for
decisions.reason: "Say" here means ask or request: clothing, jewels or anything else to win the king's favor. Esther asks for nothing beyond Hegai's advice (verse 15).

decisions.choice: go in to the king: to spend the night with him
decisions.reason: "Go in to" is the usual Hebrew way of speaking of a woman going to a man's bed (verse 14).

records.source: בָּעֶ֣רֶב׀הִ֣יא בָאָ֗ה וּ֠בַבֹּקֶר הִ֣יא שָׁבָ֞ה אֶל־בֵּ֤ית הַנָּשִׁים֙ שֵׁנִ֔י אֶל־יַ֧ד שַֽׁעֲשְׁגַ֛ז סְרִ֥יס הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ שֹׁמֵ֣ר הַפִּֽילַגְשִׁ֑ים לֹא־תָב֥וֹא עוֹד֙ אֶל־הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ כִּ֣י אִם־חָפֵ֥ץ בָּ֛הּ הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ וְנִקְרְאָ֥ה בְשֵֽׁם׃
records.gloss: In the evening she [was] going in, and in the morning she [was] returning to [the] house of the women, second, into [the] hand of Shaashgaz, eunuch of the king, keeper of the concubines; not she would go in again to the king unless delighted in her the king and she was called by name.
pieces: She would go in the evening, and in the morning she would return to the second harem, in the care of Shaashgaz, the king's eunuch who was in charge of the concubines. She would not go to the king again unless he was pleased with her and she was summoned by name.

L.14: In the evening she would go in, and in the morning she would return to the second house of the women, into the hand of Shaashgaz the king's eunuch, keeper of the concubines. She would not go in to the king again unless the king delighted in her and she was summoned by name.

R.14: She went to the king in the evening, and in the morning she went back to a different part of the women's quarters. There Shaashgaz, the king's official, was in charge of the concubines, the king's secondary wives. She did not go to the king again unless he was pleased with her and asked for her by name.

decisions.choice: concubines: women who belonged to the king as secondary wives
decisions.reason: A concubine had a lower rank than a wife. After one night with the king, a young woman became one of his concubines and lived in the second house, often never to be called again.

decisions.choice: the house of the women, second: a second harem, or a second time to the harem
alternatives: she returned a second time to the house of the women
decisions.reason: The word "second" stands after "house of the women" and can describe the house (a second harem, for the concubines) or the return. Since Shaashgaz is in charge of the concubines, a separate house is likely.

decisions.choice: delighted in her ... called by name: only if the king wanted her again
decisions.reason: To be called by name is to be summoned personally. The same rule appears from Esther's side in 4:11.

decisions.choice: the king's secondary wives (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable explains "concubine" the first time in the chapter, as the project does elsewhere.

records.source: וּבְהַגִּ֣יעַ תֹּר־אֶסְתֵּ֣ר בַּת־אֲבִיחַ֣יִל דֹּ֣ד מָרְדֳּכַ֡י אֲשֶׁר֩ לָקַֽח־ל֨וֹ לְבַ֜ת לָב֣וֹא אֶל־הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ לֹ֤א בִקְשָׁה֙ דָּבָ֔ר כִּ֠י אִ֣ם אֶת־אֲשֶׁ֥ר יֹאמַ֛ר הֵגַ֥י סְרִיס־הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ שֹׁמֵ֣ר הַנָּשִׁ֑ים וַתְּהִ֤י אֶסְתֵּר֙ נֹשֵׂ֣את חֵ֔ן בְּעֵינֵ֖י כָּל־רֹאֶֽיהָ׃
records.gloss: And when arrived [the] turn of Esther, daughter of Abihail, uncle of Mordecai, who had taken her for himself as a daughter, to go in to the king, not she asked [for] a thing except what said Hegai, eunuch of the king, keeper of the women. And was Esther winning favor in [the] eyes of all who saw her.
pieces: When the turn came for Esther, the daughter of Abihail, Mordecai's uncle, who had adopted her as his daughter, to go in to the king, she asked for nothing except what Hegai the king's eunuch, who was in charge of the women, advised. And Esther won the favor of everyone who saw her.

L.15: And when the turn came of Esther the daughter of Abihail, the uncle of Mordecai, who had taken her for himself as a daughter, to go in to the king, she did not ask for anything except what Hegai the king's eunuch, keeper of the women, said. And Esther was winning favor in the eyes of all who saw her.

R.15: Esther was the daughter of Abihail, Mordecai's uncle, and Mordecai had adopted her. When it was her turn to go to the king, she asked only for the things that Hegai, the king's official in charge of the women, suggested. Everyone who saw Esther liked her.

decisions.choice: she asked for nothing except what Hegai said: she trusted his advice
decisions.reason: Unlike others who took whatever they wished (verse 13), Esther relied on Hegai, who knew the king's tastes. The text presents this as wisdom and modesty.

decisions.choice: winning favor in the eyes of: being liked and approved by
decisions.reason: The phrase is used of Joseph (Genesis 39:4, 21) and Ruth (Ruth 2:10); Esther wins favor again and again (2:9, 17; 5:2, 8).

decisions.choice: Abihail, uncle of Mordecai: Esther's father
decisions.reason: The full name of her father is given at the moment of her great test, as in 9:29. Esther and Mordecai are cousins (verse 7).

decisions.choice: everyone who saw her (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: "Everyone" is already inclusive in English, so no gender setting is used.

records.source: וַתִּלָּקַ֨ח אֶסְתֵּ֜ר אֶל־הַמֶּ֤לֶךְ אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ֙ אֶל־בֵּ֣ית מַלְכוּת֔וֹ בַּחֹ֥דֶשׁ הָעֲשִׂירִ֖י הוּא־חֹ֣דֶשׁ טֵבֵ֑ת בִּשְׁנַת־שֶׁ֖בַע לְמַלְכוּתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And was taken Esther to the king Ahasuerus, to [the] house of his royalty, in the month the tenth, that [is the] month Tebeth, in year seven of his reign.
pieces: Esther was taken to King Ahasuerus in his royal palace in the tenth month, which is the month Tebeth, in the seventh year of his reign.

L.16: And Esther was taken to King Ahasuerus, to his royal house, in the tenth month, which is the month Tebeth, in the seventh year of his reign.

R.16: So Esther was taken to King Ahasuerus in his royal palace. It was in the tenth month, the month of Tebeth, in the middle of winter, during the seventh year of his rule.

decisions.choice: the tenth month, the month Tebeth: about December to January
decisions.reason: The months are counted from the spring, and their Babylonian names were used by the Jews after the exile (Ezra and Nehemiah do the same). Tebeth falls in midwinter.

decisions.choice: the seventh year of his reign: the winter of 479-478 BC, four years after the feast of 1:3
decisions.reason: If Ahasuerus is Xerxes, his seventh year began in spring 479 BC, so Tebeth fell at the turn of 479 and 478 BC. Greek historians place his great campaign against Greece (480-479 BC) between the third and seventh years, which may explain the gap, though the text says nothing of it.

decisions.choice: in the middle of winter (Readable)
decisions.reason: As the term list for Esther allows, Readable adds the season so the date means something to a modern reader.

records.source: וַיֶּאֱהַ֨ב הַמֶּ֤לֶךְ אֶת־אֶסְתֵּר֙ מִכָּל־הַנָּשִׁ֔ים וַתִּשָּׂא־חֵ֥ן וָחֶ֛סֶד לְפָנָ֖יו מִכָּל־הַבְּתוּלֹ֑ת וַיָּ֤שֶׂם כֶּֽתֶר־מַלְכוּת֙ בְּרֹאשָׁ֔הּ וַיַּמְלִיכֶ֖הָ תַּ֥חַת וַשְׁתִּֽי׃
records.gloss: And loved the king Esther more than all the women, and she won favor and kindness before him more than all the virgins; and he set [the] crown of royalty on her head and made her queen instead of Vashti.
pieces: The king loved Esther more than all the other women, and she won his favor and approval more than any of the other virgins. So he set the royal crown on her head and made her queen instead of Vashti.

L.17: And the king loved Esther more than all the women, and she won favor and kindness before him more than all the virgins, and he set the royal crown on her head and made her queen instead of Vashti.

R.17: The king loved Esther more than any of the other women. He liked her and was kinder to her than to any of the other young women. So he put the royal crown on her head and made her queen in Vashti's place.

decisions.choice: favor and kindness: his full goodwill
decisions.reason: The two words are paired to stress how completely she pleased him. As in verse 9, chesed here is a superior's goodwill, not covenant love.

decisions.choice: crown of royalty ... instead of Vashti: the end of chapter 1 reversed
decisions.reason: Vashti was summoned to appear "with the crown of royalty" (1:11) and lost her place (1:19); now the same crown is set on Esther "instead of Vashti", as the counselors proposed (2:4).

decisions.choice: favor and kindness (Literal); favor and approval (Balanced); liked her and was kinder to her (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 9, the project's usual wording for chesed would mislead here; Balanced and Readable say what the pair means.

records.source: וַיַּ֨עַשׂ הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ מִשְׁתֶּ֣ה גָד֗וֹל לְכָל־שָׂרָיו֙ וַעֲבָדָ֔יו אֵ֖ת מִשְׁתֵּ֣ה אֶסְתֵּ֑ר וַהֲנָחָ֤ה לַמְּדִינוֹת֙ עָשָׂ֔ה וַיִּתֵּ֥ן מַשְׂאֵ֖ת כְּיַ֥ד הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃
records.gloss: And made the king a feast great for all his princes and his servants, the feast of Esther; and a release to the provinces he made, and he gave gifts according to [the] hand of the king.
pieces: Then the king gave a great banquet for all his officials and servants, the banquet in honor of Esther. He also declared a release from taxes for the provinces and gave gifts with royal generosity.

L.18: And the king made a great feast for all his princes and his servants, the feast of Esther, and he made a release for the provinces and gave gifts according to the hand of the king.

R.18: Then the king gave a great feast for all his leaders and officials to honor Esther. He gave the provinces a break from paying taxes, and he gave generous gifts, as only a king could.

decisions.choice: a release: a remission of taxes, or a holiday
decisions.reason: The word is found only here and comes from the root "rest". It may mean a rest from taxes or labor, a public holiday, or a release of prisoners; Persian kings were known to remit taxes at the start of a reign. The general sense is a royal favor to the whole empire.

decisions.choice: the feast of Esther: a new feast for a new queen
decisions.reason: The book began with a feast that ended with the loss of a queen (chapter 1); this feast celebrates the new one. Feasts frame the whole story (9:17-19).

decisions.choice: according to the hand of the king: with royal generosity
decisions.reason: As in 1:7, the hand stands for the king's wealth and power.

decisions.choice: princes, servants (Literal); officials, servants (Balanced); leaders, officials (Readable)
decisions.reason: The wording for sar and for the king's servants follows 1:3.

records.source: וּבְהִקָּבֵ֥ץ בְּתוּל֖וֹת שֵׁנִ֑ית וּמָרְדֳּכַ֖י יֹשֵׁ֥ב בְּשַֽׁעַר־הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃
records.gloss: And when were gathered virgins a second [time], and Mordecai [was] sitting in [the] gate of the king.
pieces: When the virgins were gathered together a second time, Mordecai was sitting at the king's gate.

L.19: And when the virgins were gathered a second time, Mordecai was sitting in the gate of the king.

R.19: Later, when the young women were gathered again, Mordecai was serving as an official at the king's gate.

decisions.choice: when virgins were gathered a second time: the reason for the second gathering is not given
alternatives: when the virgins were assembled again (for another purpose)
decisions.reason: The clause is hard to explain. It may refer to a second gathering of young women after Esther was made queen, to the women moving to the second house (verse 14), or to a later event the narrator does not explain. The old Greek translation leaves the phrase out. What matters for the story is the time setting for Mordecai's discovery in verses 21-23.

decisions.choice: sitting in the king's gate: holding a post at the palace
decisions.reason: The gate complex of a palace was where officials did business and justice was given (Ruth 4:1; Daniel 2:49). Mordecai sits there again in verse 21, in 3:2-3 and in 5:13; the phrase means he served at court, not that he waited outside.

decisions.choice: serving as an official at the king's gate (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable says what "sitting" there meant.

records.source: אֵ֣ין אֶסְתֵּ֗ר מַגֶּ֤דֶת מֽוֹלַדְתָּהּ֙ וְאֶת־עַמָּ֔הּ כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר צִוָּ֥ה עָלֶ֖יהָ מָרְדֳּכָ֑י וְאֶת־מַאֲמַ֤ר מָרְדֳּכַי֙ אֶסְתֵּ֣ר עֹשָׂ֔ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר הָיְתָ֥ה בְאָמְנָ֖ה אִתּֽוֹ׃ס
records.gloss: Not Esther [was] telling her kindred and her people, as had commanded her Mordecai; and the word of Mordecai Esther [was] doing, as when she was in guardianship with him.
pieces: Esther still had not revealed her family background or her nationality, just as Mordecai had instructed her. She continued to follow Mordecai's instructions as she had done when he was bringing her up.

L.20: Esther was not making known her kindred or her people, as Mordecai had commanded her; and Esther did what Mordecai said, just as when she was being brought up by him.

R.20: Esther still had not told anyone about her family or that she was Jewish, because Mordecai had told her not to. She still obeyed Mordecai, just as she had when he was raising her.

decisions.choice: Esther was not telling: she still kept the secret, even as queen
decisions.reason: The verse repeats verse 10 to show that queenship had not changed Esther's obedience to Mordecai. The secret prepares for 7:3-4.

decisions.choice: guardianship: the time he was bringing her up
decisions.reason: The noun is related to the verb in verse 7 and occurs only here.

records.source: בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֔ם וּמָרְדֳּכַ֖י יֹשֵׁ֣ב בְּשַֽׁעַר־הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ קָצַף֩ בִּגְתָ֨ן וָתֶ֜רֶשׁ שְׁנֵֽי־סָרִיסֵ֤י הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ מִשֹּׁמְרֵ֣י הַסַּ֔ף וַיְבַקְשׁוּ֙ לִשְׁלֹ֣חַ יָ֔ד בַּמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֲחַשְׁוֵֽרֹשׁ׃
records.gloss: In the days the those, and Mordecai [was] sitting in [the] gate of the king, was angry Bigthan and Teresh, two [of the] eunuchs of the king, from [the] keepers of the threshold, and they sought to send a hand against the king Ahasuerus.
pieces: In those days, while Mordecai was sitting at the king's gate, Bigthan and Teresh, two of the king's eunuchs who guarded the doorway, became angry and plotted to assassinate King Ahasuerus.

L.21: In those days, while Mordecai was sitting in the gate of the king, Bigthan and Teresh, two of the king's eunuchs from the keepers of the threshold, became angry and sought to lay a hand on King Ahasuerus.

R.21: During that time, while Mordecai was serving at the king's gate, two of the king's officials became angry with the king. They were Bigthan and Teresh, who guarded the doors to the king's rooms. They made plans to kill King Ahasuerus.

decisions.choice: keepers of the threshold: guards of the doors to the king's private rooms
decisions.reason: These were trusted servants with close access to the king, which made their plot dangerous. The same title is used for temple officials in 2 Kings 12:10.

decisions.choice: to send a hand against the king: to kill him
decisions.reason: To stretch out or send a hand against someone is to attack him (1 Samuel 24:7; 26:9). Xerxes was in fact murdered by members of his own court in 465 BC, though not by these men.

decisions.choice: was angry: the cause of their anger is not given
decisions.reason: The text gives no reason; the story needs only the plot and Mordecai's discovery of it.

decisions.choice: eunuchs (Literal, Balanced); officials (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 1:10.

records.heading: Mordecai uncovers a plot against the king

records.source: וַיִּוָּדַ֤ע הַדָּבָר֙ לְמָרְדֳּכַ֔י וַיַּגֵּ֖ד לְאֶסְתֵּ֣ר הַמַּלְכָּ֑ה וַתֹּ֧אמֶר אֶסְתֵּ֛ר לַמֶּ֖לֶךְ בְּשֵׁ֥ם מָרְדֳּכָֽי׃
records.gloss: And was made known the matter to Mordecai, and he told [it] to Esther the queen, and said Esther to the king in [the] name of Mordecai.
pieces: Mordecai learned of the plot and told Queen Esther, and Esther told the king, giving Mordecai the credit.

L.22: And the matter became known to Mordecai, and he told [it] to Esther the queen, and Esther spoke to the king in the name of Mordecai.

R.22: Mordecai found out about the plan and told Queen Esther. Then Esther warned the king and told him that the news came from Mordecai.

decisions.choice: in the name of Mordecai: saying that Mordecai had discovered it
decisions.reason: Esther passed on the warning and made sure it was credited to Mordecai. This is what is found written in the royal records in 6:1-2.

decisions.choice: was made known: how Mordecai learned of it is not said
decisions.reason: The passive verb leaves open how the plot came to his ears.

records.source: וַיְבֻקַּ֤שׁ הַדָּבָר֙ וַיִּמָּצֵ֔א וַיִּתָּל֥וּ שְׁנֵיהֶ֖ם עַל־עֵ֑ץ וַיִּכָּתֵ֗ב בְּסֵ֛פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י הַיָּמִ֖ים לִפְנֵ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃פ
records.gloss: And was investigated the matter, and it was found, and were hanged [the] two of them on a tree; and it was written in [the] book of [the] matters of the days before the king.
pieces: The matter was investigated and found to be true, and both men were hanged on a gallows. And this was recorded in the book of the annals in the king's presence.

L.23: And the matter was investigated and found [true], and the two of them were hanged on a tree. And it was written in the book of the chronicles before the king.

R.23: The king's officers looked into the matter and found that it was true. So both men were put to death and hanged on a pole. All this was written down in the king's official record book.

decisions.choice: hanged on a tree: put to death and displayed on a wooden pole
decisions.reason: The word for "tree" means wood, a tree or a pole. The Persians were known to impale condemned men on stakes, and the Hebrew verb "hang" can describe that or the hanging up of a body after death (Deuteronomy 21:22-23). The same word is used for the "gallows" Haman builds (5:14; 7:9-10).

decisions.choice: the book of the matters of the days: the royal chronicles
decisions.reason: Persian kings kept written records of events and of those who had served the king (6:1-2; Ezra 4:15). The record of Mordecai's deed, unrewarded for now, becomes the turning point of the story in chapter 6.

decisions.choice: before the king: in the king's presence, or by his order
decisions.reason: "Before the king" may mean that the record was made in his presence or simply that it was entered in the king's own records.

decisions.choice: tree (Literal); gallows (Balanced); put to death and hanged on a pole (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced uses "gallows" as in 5:14 and 7:9-10, so the reader sees the link. Readable says plainly that the men were executed, since a wooden pole was used to display the body or to impale the condemned.
